newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone 1996 net income up eight percent.
newsitem.headline: Danone 1996 net income up eight percent.

text.p: (Figures in millions of French francs unless stated)

NOTE - Danone said in a statement net income rose more than the operating income due mainly to lower interest rates. It restated the 1995 comparative figures for an exceptional restructuring charge of 1.8 billion, which was 997 million after tax. The published 1995 net income figure was 2,133 million.

"Danone Group's net income for 1996 rose by eight percent, outstripping projections made during the year," it said in a statement. "Operating income increased 6.5 percent on sales up 5.7 percent, reflecting a rise in the group's operating margin."

Its operating margin rose to 8.9 percent from 8.8 percent in 1995, reflecting improvements in European activities -- 9.3 percent versus 9.1 percent -- and in international activities, six percent in 1996 compared with 5.6 percent.

The ratio of operating income to sales rose to 10.2 percent from 9.6 percent in dairy products, declined to 6.3 percent from 6.4 percent in grocery products and pasta, rose to seven percent from 6.7 percent in biscuits, to 13.6 percent from 12.4 percent in mineral water, and to 11.2 percent from 10 percent in containers. It fell to 11.7 percent from 13 percent for beer.
